question: My phone was stolen and I received an unexpected MFA prompt. What must happen?
actual_answer: If you received an unexpected MFA prompt after your phone was stolen, you must report the incident immediately. The old authenticator registration will be revoked once your identity is verified, and the Help Desk will record the loss [SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices]. Additionally, since you reported an unexpected MFA prompt, security escalation is mandatory [SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices]. Be sure to contact the Help Desk through an approved corporate channel to initiate this process [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow].
reference_answer: After identity is verified, revoke the stolen device's authenticator registration as soon as possible and record the loss in the ticket. Advise the employee to report suspected compromise to Security Operations. Because an unexpected MFA prompt was reported, Security escalation is mandatory and the case also receives the Security Review classification.

question: What information must the Help Desk record in an MFA recovery ticket?
actual_answer:
The Help Desk must record the following information in an MFA recovery ticket:

- Employee identifier
- Corporate contact channel
- Affected payroll function
- Deadline if any
- Device-loss status
- Verification methods attempted
- Verification outcome
- Old-authenticator revocation status
- Re-enrolment outcome
- Retrieved policy version
- Every escalation made

It is important to note that passwords, OTP values, full identity numbers, banking PINs, or recovery secrets must not be included in the ticket [OPS-09::required-ticket-fields]. Additionally, the old authenticator registration must be revoked as soon as identity is verified if a device is reported lost or stolen [SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices].
reference_answer: Record the employee identifier, corporate contact channel, affected payroll function, deadline if any, device-loss status, verification methods attempted, verification outcome, old-authenticator revocation status, re-enrolment outcome, retrieved policy version, and every escalation. Do not record passwords, OTP values, full identity numbers, banking PINs, or recovery secrets.

question: I changed phones and cannot complete MFA. How do I regain payroll access?
actual_answer:
To regain payroll access after changing phones and being unable to complete MFA, you need to contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel. The Help Desk will verify your identity, revoke the unavailable authenticator, and initiate the device re-enrolment process. You must complete the new enrolment before normal payroll access is restored [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow].

After successful identity verification, the Help Desk will revoke the old authenticator and issue a single-use enrolment link to your corporate account. You must register the new device and complete a test sign-in to finalize the recovery [SEC-17::device-re-enrolment]. 

Make sure the identity verification includes your employee identifier and two approved factors from your identity record [SEC-17::identity-verification].
reference_answer: Contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel. After identity verification succeeds, the Help Desk revokes the unavailable authenticator and starts device re-enrolment. A single-use enrolment link is sent to the corporate account and expires after 30 minutes. Register the new device and complete a successful test sign-in; recovery is complete only after that test succeeds. If required verification fails, recovery must stop and be escalated.

question: An assisted payroll change is complete, but the new-device test sign-in failed. Can the MFA recovery ticket be closed?
actual_answer: The MFA recovery ticket cannot be closed because the test sign-in has failed. According to the policy, the MFA recovery can only be closed after the old registration is revoked, the new device is enrolled, and the test sign-in is successful [OPS-09::closure-evidence]. Since the test sign-in was unsuccessful, the process is still incomplete and the ticket must remain open [SEC-17::device-re-enrolment].
reference_answer: No. Close the MFA recovery only after the old registration is recorded as revoked, the new device as enrolled, and the test sign-in as successful. Completing an assisted payroll submission may close the urgent payroll task, but it does not close an unfinished MFA recovery.
